paths.description: Entry/home and listing archetype; represents global chrome, category grids, ads, preferences, performance and mobile layout.
Search-results archetype and core content-discovery journey.
Primary account-creation form, including empty submission and input-assistance review.

findings.summary: Dark appearance is manual-only and ignores the system preference.
findings.evidence: The screenshot captured under prefers-color-scheme: dark remains white/blue; recon shows a manual “다크” button but no preference-driven retint.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and initialize surface/text colors from prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while retaining the manual override.

findings.summary: Advertising overwhelms the primary content and navigation.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, after the header and search, the entire first scroll region is a dense two-column grid of gambling banners; content cards begin far below.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or sharply limit above-the-fold ad inventory, label ads, reserve a small bounded slot, and put content/navigation first.

findings.summary: Route and state changes use abrupt legacy navigation with no transition or attention cue.
findings.evidence: Recon found no View Transition CSS/API use; navigation is conventional full-page links and the page contains no transition animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation with a reduced-motion fallback and directional cues for category/detail changes.

findings.summary: Failure and invalid-form states do not provide actionable recovery.
findings.evidence: An unknown URL silently becomes the indexed homepage, and submitting the empty registration form leaves the form unchanged with no visible inline error or recovery explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 page with useful links; validate registration after interaction, identify each invalid field, move focus to an error summary, and announce it via aria-live.

findings.summary: Contrast and preference-aware control visibility are insufficient.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility is 0.57 and its color-contrast audit fails; increased-contrast capture does not introduce a distinct high-contrast treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text/control contrast to WCAG AA, preserve visible boundaries in forced colors, and add prefers-contrast/forced-colors adjustments.

findings.summary: The page is slow, unstable and extremely heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports performance 0.41, LCP 6.8s and CLS 0.395. HAR records 152 requests and 12.97 MB, including 11.35 MB images. The image audit finds all 100 images without complete dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, remove most above-fold ad images, serve responsive AVIF/WebP, lazy-load below-fold assets, subset fonts, and eliminate the redirect hop.

findings.summary: Interactive elements and media lack accessible names, labels, structure and adequate target sizing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags the icon-only search button without an accessible name; probes find login/search controls without labels, many targets only 14–22px high, an empty H1, and 27 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels and button names, meaningful alt text, a non-empty H1 and logical landmarks; enlarge touch targets to at least 24px and preferably 44px.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party delivery are disproportionate and not visibly consent-minimised.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence finds Google Tag Manager/Analytics and six third-party origins; HAR records 151 requests as third-party relative to the requested redirect origin and 20 analytics requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit and remove non-essential tags, delay optional analytics until consent, batch events, and document retention/purpose close to collection.

findings.summary: Crawler and indexing endpoints produce soft-home responses and inconsistent canonical signals.
findings.evidence: robots.txt and sitemap.xml both redirect to mingky05.live and return the homepage HTML; an unknown route also becomes the indexable canonical homepage instead of a 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve valid text/plain robots.txt and XML sitemap responses, return HTTP 404 for unknown routes, and keep canonical URLs aligned with each actual resource.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS but finds no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; test in report-only first.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and does not expose phishing-resistant sign-in.
findings.evidence: Recon and registration probes show only identifier/password account controls and no WebAuthn or passkey surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication, retaining a secure recovery path and password fallback during migration.

findings.summary: HTTP failures are disguised as successful home navigation.
findings.evidence: Navigating to /nonexistent-audit-path ends at / with normal homepage content, index,follow and canonical /; no missing-page explanation or retry/back path is shown.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the failed URL, return the correct HTTP status, explain what happened, and offer search, back and home recovery actions.

findings.summary: Registration validation and error handling are not humane or accessible.
findings.evidence: Registration fields are not required in HTML; after empty submit the visible form is unchanged, with no inline messages, aria-invalid state or error summary.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required and appropriate constraints, validate after interaction, add persistent field-specific messages linked with aria-describedby, and announce a summary.

findings.summary: Account inputs disable useful autocomplete and provide weak input semantics.
findings.evidence: Registration uses autocomplete=off for username and both password fields instead of username, new-password and new-password confirmation semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and autocomplete=new-password, preserve paste/password-manager support, and keep visible labels associated with each input.

findings.summary: Images and third-party media exceed a proportionate resource budget.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 11.35 MB across 103 images; the image audit reports 100 legacy-format images, 58 without srcset, 20 oversized and all without complete dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the ad/media count, generate AVIF/WebP variants and srcset/sizes, size every image, lazy-load below-fold content, and set an explicit page-weight budget.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is high for a listing page, although the repeated interaction did not show a leak.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap contains 270,609 nodes and 15.95 MB of self-size. After ten repeated search interactions growth was only 301 nodes and 47,816 bytes, so leakage was not observed, but the initial DOM/heap is large.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or paginate the very long listing, remove duplicated hidden desktop/mobile DOM, and defer below-fold card construction.

Add accessible names, labels, structure, contrast and target sizing
Deploy CSP and defensive response headers
Return truthful crawler, 404 and recovery responses
Make registration validation and autofill humane
Add modern navigation transitions and attention cues
